scope: Darwin ScreenCaptureKit capture seam and compatibility routing

commands.assertions: Configured native capture is selected before the compatibility command, and an unavailable native capture falls back through the bounded command seam. Existing capture, permission, geometry, and revoke tests remain green.
The updated native host package has no vet findings.
The non-cgo Darwin helper remains cross-compilable and keeps the compatibility path available.
The Windows helper remains cross-compilable after the capture seam change.
Native host, helper, and host-desktop integration remain race-clean after ScreenCaptureKit routing was added.
Native activation observer/image and window-process verifier interfaces are race-clean with helper and host-desktop integration.
The non-cgo Darwin helper including activation interfaces remains cross-compilable.
The Windows helper including bounded HWND/process verification remains cross-compilable.
A desktop-session transition during the native screenshot operation is rejected before image decoding or publication.

assertions: A native Darwin build wires ScreenCaptureKit through an Objective-C framework seam that captures the first permitted display frame as bounded PNG bytes.
The Go helper keeps the existing injected command seam for tests and older packaged helpers, while preferring ScreenCaptureKit when the native build provides it.
ScreenCaptureKit failure does not produce stale success; the compatibility path still requires a valid PNG and classifies empty or failed capture as permission evidence.
The native host now implements short-lived activation metadata capture, explicit image capture with virtual-screen cropping, and companion window/process verification.
Activation image evidence is refused when the captured frame cannot contain the exact probed window rectangle; no mismatched full-screen bytes are published as window evidence.
The activation image path rechecks the bound user session after capture, preventing pixels from crossing a session transition.
limitations: This Linux host has no Darwin clang or Apple framework SDK, so the Objective-C cgo path could not be compiled here.
Cross-platform non-cgo packaging remains on the compatibility path; a Darwin release helper must be built with the Apple SDK and cgo enabled before claiming packaged ScreenCaptureKit delivery.
No macOS user-session, Screen Recording permission, grant/revoke, or artifact journey was available; NAT-04 and the macOS support row remain unverified.
The Darwin ScreenCaptureKit cgo path still requires Apple clang and SDK on a macOS build host; Linux can only validate the non-cgo compatibility build.
macOS verifier checks the companion process through the Accessibility session; native NSView-to-window-number verification still requires an Apple-host integration test.
